scenarios.name: eslint-prettier-on-staged-files
scenarios.rationale: Both install the packages, run `npx husky init`, write a plain-command pre-commit hook, and note that `prepare` activates hooks for teammates; B follows the rubric more closely with `lint-staged` as a plain command and the exact `*.{ts,tsx}` mapping, while A uses `npx lint-staged` and a broader glob (still acceptable) and adds extra config and a `--max-warnings` flag beyond what was asked.

scenarios.name: monorepo-subfolder-hooks
scenarios.rationale: Both give the correct prepare script and the hook with cd frontend and explain that Git runs hooks from the repo root; B shows the hook as a two-line file and states the explanation more directly with the hook location, while A mentions the explanation up front and puts the hook in a single line, so both cover the rubric and B is slightly more complete and explicit.

scenarios.name: ci-skip-and-commit-msg-validation
scenarios.rationale: A covers all three rubric points (the exact `npx --no -- commitlint --edit $1` hook, `HUSKY=0` for Docker/CI, `-n` to skip) and says hooks can't be relied on so the checks should also run in CI, while B quotes `"$1"`, never states the CI-enforcement caveat, and leaves the setup unapplied awaiting approval, though it does cover `HUSKY=0` and `-n`/`--no-verify`.
